title: OPP officer cleared in shooting death
subtitle: (KAWARTHA LAKES) The Special Investigations Unit (SIU) has cleared an OPP officer of any wrongdoing following their investigation into the shooting death of 41-year-old Anthony Parro near Kirkfield Feb. 7.
article: (KAWARTHA LAKES) The Special Investigations Unit (SIU) has cleared an OPP officer of any wrongdoing following their investigation into the shooting death of 41-year-old Anthony Parro near Kirkfield Feb. 7.
In a press release, the SIU stated that, on the day of the shooting, police received a number of complaints of a pickup truck being driven erratically.
A lone officer, driving in a marked cruiser, caught up with the 2003 GMC Sierra pickup as it was travelling north on Kirkfield Road.

The SIU says Mr. Parro, of Oshawa, eventually stopped the truck in the southbound lane of the road, followed by the cruiser, but started backing up towards the police vehicle, forcing the officer to back up to avoid a crash.

At some point, Mr. Parro began driving forward at which time the officer tried to follow, but his vehicle stalled. When the officer got the cruiser started again and was about to pursue the truck, it started reversing again, gaining speed as it came at the cruiser, forcing the officer to get out.

The SIU stated the officer removed his gun from its holster as the truck smashed into the front of the cruiser, causing extensive damage and forcing it backwards. When the officer was slightly in front of the truck, Mr. Parro again put the truck in drive and accelerated, at which time the officer shot his gun seven times at Mr. Parro; twice before the truck passed him and the remaining five as it was passing him, or just past him.
Mr. Parro was shot twice in the right arm, once in the lower left side and once on the left side of his neck, the release states.
The truck then veered onto the left side of the roadway while accelerating before stopping in a field because of extensive damage.
Mr. Parro was pronounced dead at the scene.

"In my view, the subject officer was justified in his use of lethal force in these circumstances. Mr. Parro had already made two concerted attempts to strike the officer's vehicle with the back of his truck. Immediately after the second attempt, the subject officer was standing outside of his cruiser slightly ahead of the truck, on the driver's side. In this position, the subject officer could have reasonably concluded Mr. Parro was trying to run him over when he accelerated forward," stated Ian Scott, director of the SIU.

"The fact that some of the firearm discharges took place after the front of the pickup truck had already passed the subject officer does not in my view detract from the officer's subjective view of imminent danger; other bullet trajectories and locations of the bullet casings strongly suggest that the subject officer's first two discharges took place at a moment when Mr. Parro could have steered his pickup truck directly at the subject officer. Given the two previous attempts to ram the police cruiser, I am of the view that the officer had a reasonable apprehension of imminent death or serious bodily harm at the critical moment when Mr. Parro accelerated. Accordingly, he had the lawful authority to use lethal force in these circumstances," Mr. Scott stated in the release.

Six SIU investigators were assigned to look into the case, including interviews with eight officers and 14 civilian witnesses. The officer in question provided his duty notes to the SIU, but declined an interview with investigators, as is his legal right, the release states.

"Because he did not provide an oral statement and the investigators did not have an opportunity to ask any questions about the preparation of the notes, I am not inclined to place much weight on them. However, with respect to this incident, there is enough information in the form of civilian witnesses, contemporaneous radio communications captured on tape from the subject officer, and forensic reports to reconstruct the material events," added Mr. Scott.
The SIU investigates reports involving police where there has been a death, serious injury or allegations of sexual assault.
